text:
maya: Heads-up — ran an nsys trace and found a regressing matmul path when KV-cache is warm. baseline cold-KV token latency ~12.3ms, after recent change it's ~27-30ms :eyes:

raj: can you paste the nsys command and the top kernel timeline lines?

maya: command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn -o 1753209874_run1 -- python serve_bench.py --model rlhf-v1 --batch 4
```
Top timeline snippet from the report (aggregate):
```
cuBLASLt_matmul    -> 82.3ms  (dominant, alg id 7, workspace 96MB)
cublas_gemm        -> 12.8ms  (what we saw before)
kv_cache_copy      -> 3.5ms
other kernels...
```
Selector is now picking the cuBLASLt path for these shapes after the recent matmul heuristics tweak.

oscar: hmm, alg id 7 requiring ~96MB workspace is notable — do we ever set cublasLtAttrAlgoMaxWorkspace or allocate a workspace buffer? if not lt will sometimes fallback at runtime and that can be very slow.

maya: we don't set a global workspace today. runtime passes workspace=null and leaves selection to cuBLASLt. I suspect the selector toggled to report "lt-friendly" shapes and lt picks an algo that expects a workspace; because we don't provide one it goes into a slower fallback path. also the matmul dims change between prefix/first-token (S=1,B=4) vs steady-state (S=64,B=1) so heuristics mis-classify steady work.

zoe: also consider batching heuristics — when requests are merged we switch to a different matmul shape, and KV warm vs cold creates two regimes. :thinking: could be an interplay between batching thresholds and kv-cache warmup.

raj: quick repro idea: force max workspace=0 vs force 96MB and compare. also enable cublasLt logging (cublasLtSetDescriptorAttribute + print alg choices) to see why alg id 7 picked.

maya: ran both hacks: forcing max workspace=0 -> latency back to ~13.1ms. forcing 96MB allocation -> 11.8ms but memory usage spikes and one of our smaller instance types OOMs. so it's faster if you give the workspace, but not viable for all customers.

oscar: two possible fixes: 1) change selector to prefer workspace-free algos when free GPU mem < threshold, or 2) implement a shared workspace pool with LRU so we can reuse the buffer without per-request alloc/free overhead.

zoe: also check the quantized matmul path — 8-bit kernels may route through a different GEMM kernel; recent commit 2f4b touched that code path and I saw a perf regression in unit perf tests too. worth comparing traces with int8 vs fp16.

maya: agreed. action items: (1) I'll produce a minimal repro that forces alg choices and upload full qdrep, (2) raj to PR a small selector tweak that consults free GPU memory and prefers low-workspace algos if mem low, (3) oscar to prototype lightweight workspace pool. I'll also attach the nsys flames in a followup.

infra-bot: profile uploaded -> https://s3.redwood-inference/internal-profiles/1753209874_run1.qdrep

raj: ack. I'll add a perf test for the two regimes (cold-KV vs warm-KV) so we don't regress again.

maya: thanks — will follow up with the repro and the screenshots. :thumbsup:
